Response to Show Cause Order 
 
Dear Secretary Reese: 
 
 
Pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”),1 Part 35 of the Federal Energy 
Regulatory Commission’s (the “Commission”) regulations and Rules 209 and 213 of the 
Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure,2 GridLiance West LLC (“GridLiance West”) 
respectfully submits this response to the Commission’s Show Cause Order issued pursuant to 
section 206 of the FPA on June 18, 2026, in Docket No. EL26-71-000 directing the California 
Independent System Operator Corporation (“CAISO”) and Participating Transmission Owners 
(“PTOs”) in CAISO to show cause why their tariffs are just and reasonable and not unduly 
discriminatory or preferential, or in the alternative to explain the necessary changes to remedy 
the Commission’s identified concerns.3  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission also 
encouraged a response in the form of a section 205 filing proposing tariff revisions remedying 
the concerns identified in the Show Cause Order.4  
 
In the instant filing, GridLiance West proposes revisions to its Transmission Owner Tariff 
(“GridLiance West Tariff”)5 and supporting explanations in response to the Show Cause Order to 
remedy the concerns identified therein.  GridLiance West’s proposed tariff revisions are just and

certain aspects of the Show Cause Order are not applicable to GridLiance West due to its role as 
a Non-Load-Serving Entity PTO (“Non-LSE PTO”).6  Thus, GridLiance West requests that the 
show cause proceeding be terminated with respect to GridLiance West.  
Further, GridLiance West respectfully requests a 30-day comment period on this filing.  
GridLiance West also respectfully requests that the Commission accept the amendments 
proposed herein effective February 16, 2027. The requested dates align with those requested by 
CAISO.  
 
I. 
BACKGROUND  
A. 
GridLiance West 
 
GridLiance West operates transmission facilities within CAISO. GridLiance West is a 
Delaware limited liability company and a wholly owned subsidiary of NextEra Energy 
Transmission, LLC. GridLiance West owns and operates the High Voltage Transmission System 
(“HVTS”) previously owned by Valley Electric Transmission Association, LLC, a wholly owned 
subsidiary of Valley Electric Association, Inc. The HVTS consists of approximately 165 miles of 
230-kV transmission lines and related substation infrastructure that runs through rural Southern 
Nevada. The HVTS has been incorporated into the CAISO-controlled grid, and GridLiance West 
is a Non-LSE PTO in CAISO. 
 
 
GridLiance West recovers its transmission revenue requirement (“TRR”) through a 
Commission-approved formula rate under the GridLiance West Tariff, which is invoiced and 
collected through the CAISO Access Charge rates under Section 26 of the CAISO Open Access 
Transmission Tariff (“CAISO Tariff”).  As a Non-LSE PTO under the CAISO Tariff and 
Transmission Control Agreement,7 GridLiance West serves no retail load.8 
B. 
Show Cause Order 
 
On June 18, 2026, the Commission initiated a show cause proceeding against CAISO and 
the PTOs pursuant to section 206 of the FPA.  The Show Cause Order directed CAISO and the 
PTOs to explain why the CAISO Tariff and the Transmission Owner Tariffs of the PTOs (“PTO 
Tariffs”) remain just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential without certain 
tariff provisions addressing:9

a) the application process, study procedures, and ongoing operational requirements that 
apply to Eligible Customers10 seeking transmission service on behalf of Large Loads; 
b) additional transparency concerning the network upgrade11 costs to provide transmission 
service to Eligible Customers on behalf of Large Loads; and a pro forma cost recovery 
agreement between CAISO, the relevant transmission owner, and the Eligible Customer 
taking transmission service on behalf of the Large Load to mitigate the risk of cost 
shifting among transmission customers, and a mechanism to ensure such payments are 
appropriately credited toward transmission owners’ TRRs consistent with the 
Commission’s cost-of-service regulations; 
c) the rates, terms, and conditions of service that apply to co-location arrangements; 
d) transmission services that reflect Eligible Customers taking transmission service on 
behalf of co-located loads, load with behind the meter generation, and flexible Large 
Loads that are willing and able to limit their use of the transmission system under certain 
conditions;12 and 
e) the rates, terms, and conditions of service applicable to interconnection customers serving 
electrically proximate Large Load or co-located load. 
Alternatively, respondents may explain what changes to their tariffs would remedy the identified 
concerns if the Commission were to determine that the tariffs have in fact become unjust and 
unreasonable or unduly discriminatory or preferential and proceeds to establish a replacement 
tariff.13 
C. 
Motion for Abeyance 
 
On August 3, 2026, pursuant to Rule 212 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and 
Procedure, CAISO and the joint PTOs, which included GridLiance West, each filed motions to 
hold the above-referenced show cause proceeding in abeyance for 90 days, pending completion 
of CAISO’s stakeholder proceedings and development of the companies’ respective FPA section 
205 filings to address the Commission’s preliminary findings in the Show Cause Order

(“Abeyance Motions”).14  The Commission granted the Abeyance Motions and held this

II. 
GRIDLIANCE WEST’S PROPOSED TRANSMISSION OWNER TARIFF 
REVISIONS 
 
The proposed GridLiance West Tariff revisions are just and reasonable and not unduly 
discriminatory or preferential.  The proposed revisions establish an application process, study 
procedures, operational requirements, and creditworthiness and financial security requirements 
applicable to requests by Eligible Customers seeking to interconnect a Large Load to the 
GridLiance West transmission system.  The revisions are designed to consistently evaluate the 
reliability, operational, and planning impacts of proposed Large Loads, identify and allocate 
responsibility for any Direct Assignment Facilities, Reliability Upgrades, and other Network 
Upgrades, and mitigate the risk of cost shifting associated with the Interconnection and service 
of Large Loads.  The proposed revisions provide transparency and certainty regarding the 
information, studies, agreements, and credit and financial security commitments required from 
Eligible Customers seeking transmission service on behalf of Large Loads.16  The proposed 
amendments to the GridLiance West Tariff fall into the following categories: 
(1) 
New and revised defined terms in Section 3 of its GridLiance West Tariff, 
including definitions of Large Load, Flexible Interim Load Interconnection 
(“FILI”) Service, Interconnection Facilities, Point of Interconnection, Network 
Upgrades, Site Control, Gross Load, Transmission Revenue Requirement, and 
Reliability Upgrade; 
(2) 
Revisions to Section 5 of its GridLiance West Tariff to clarify Gross Load 
reporting associated with Large Load, consistent with the CAISO Tariff; 
(3) 
Revisions to Sections 8.1 and 10.1 through 10.17 of its GridLiance West Tariff to 
establish an interconnection application process, readiness requirements, and 
study procedures specific to Large Load interconnections; 
(4) 
Revisions to Sections 8.1.5.1, 10.12, 10.17, and 16.12 of its GridLiance West 
Tariff to establish operational and reliability requirements for Large Loads; 
(5) 
Additions to Section 10.18 of the GridLiance West Tariff to establish rates, terms, 
and conditions of service applicable to co-located Large Load and FILI Service;

(6) 
Inclusion of cost recovery, creditworthiness, and financial security provisions in 
Sections 10.11.2, 10.17.2, and 13.2.1, and including a pro forma Cost Recovery 
Agreement as a new Attachment A to the GridLiance West Tariff for the purpose

Adoption of transition provisions in Section 10.20 to protect existing and ongoing

Completed Interconnection Application before February 16, 2027. 
GridLiance West’s proposed revisions are tailored to its status as a Non-LSE PTO, are 
coordinated with and consistent with proposed CAISO Tariff revisions and satisfy the Show 
Cause Order requirements applicable to a Non-LSE PTO.  GridLiance West has also 
incorporated certain conforming and ministerial revisions, such as correcting punctuation and 
applying consistent usage of terms.  Accordingly, GridLiance West respectfully submits that the 
proposed tariff revisions are just and reasonable, not unduly discriminatory or preferential, and 
should be accepted by the Commission under section 205 of the FPA, effective as requested.  
GridLiance West further requests that the Commission terminate the show cause proceeding with 
respect to GridLiance West upon acceptance of the proposed tariff revisions. 
A. 
Large Load Interconnection Process 
In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary finding that the CAISO 
Tariff and PTO Tariffs appear to be unjust and unreasonable because they lack clear and 
consistent provisions with respect to the application and study process for Eligible Customers 
seeking transmission and interconnection service on behalf of Large Loads.17  The GridLiance 
West Tariff establishes, in Sections 8.1 and 10, a defined and time-limited interconnection 
process for Large Loads with specific application, readiness, study, and operational requirements, 
and it clarifies how a Large Load interconnected to GridLiance West’s facilities obtains 
transmission service over the CAISO Controlled Grid.  Elements of this proposal include the 
following tariff improvements for the integration of Large Loads. 
1. 
Definition of Large Load   
Commission Concerns:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the CAISO Tariff and PTO Tariffs appear to be unjust and unreasonable because they 
lack a definition of Large Load sufficient to capture loads that present the unique challenges 
described in the Show Cause Order.18 
GridLiance West Solution:  In response to the Commission’s finding, GridLiance West 
proposes to define a Large Load as “[a]n End-User located at a single site behind one or more 
Points of Interconnection to the CAISO Controlled Grid, and that has a peak load of 50 MW or 
 
17  Show Cause Order at PP 38, 49, 58.  Citations herein to the “GridLiance West Tariff” refer to the revised 
GridLiance West TO Tariff included as Appendices A and B to this filing.  Citations to the “CAISO Proposed Tariff” 
refer to the tariff revisions CAISO is submitting contemporaneously in response to the Show Cause Order. 
18  Show Cause Order at PP 56, 57.

6 
greater.”19 This definition is identical to the definition CAISO proposes to add to Appendix A of 
the CAISO Tariff, and adopts the 50 MW threshold the Commission identified as reasonable.20  
GridLiance West has also adopted CAISO’s approach of not excluding co-located loads from the 
definition of Large Load to ensure alignment between the two tariffs. 
2. 
Application and Study Procedures 
Commission Concerns:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the CAISO Tariff and PTO Tariffs appear to be unjust and unreasonable because they 
lack clear and consistent provisions addressing the application process and study procedures for 
Eligible Customers to request transmission service on behalf of Large Loads.21  The Commission 
indicated that such processes should clarify that applications be accepted on a rolling basis; 
require a non-refundable application fee as well as staged readiness requirements; and specify 
the information and data requirements to be submitted with an application.22 
GridLiance West Solution:  The proposed tariff revisions leverage GridLiance West’s 
existing application and study processes while identifying the additional procedures applicable to 
Large Loads due to their unique operational requirements and reliability impacts on the 
transmission system.  GridLiance West submits that this approach promotes transparency and 
administrative efficiency by providing a single, integrated framework for Large Load 
interconnection requests under the GridLiance West Tariff.  This is responsive to the Show Cause 
Order’s concern regarding the lack of specificity for Large Loads and their unique operational 
characteristics and requirements. 
GridLiance West’s proposed tariff revisions establish the applicable provisions for 
Eligible Customers requesting service on behalf of Large Loads (as defined in the GridLiance 
West Tariff).  First, revised Section 8.1 explicitly extends GridLiance West’s obligation to 
interconnect to entities eligible to request interconnection pursuant to FPA section 210(a) and 
Eligible Customers, including Large Loads owned or served by a third party.  Because 
GridLiance West is a Non-LSE PTO with no retail customers, a Large Load connecting directly 
to GridLiance West’s facilities may not qualify as an “Eligible Customer” in certain instances.  
GridLiance West therefore proposes, in new Section 10.2, a voluntary offer of unbundled retail 
transmission service, where consistent with state law, so that Large Loads can request 
Interconnection and be studied under the GridLiance West Tariff as the Show Cause Order 
contemplates.23 Second, revised Section 10.1 requires that a Large Load Interconnection be 
requested pursuant to Section 10 of the GridLiance West Tariff and comply with Section 25.7 of

are accepted on a rolling basis, and revised Section 10.4 requires GridLiance West to timestamp 
each Large Load Interconnection Application to establish study priority on a rolling basis.  
Consistent with the Commission’s concern that the tariffs specify which entity is 
responsible for the study, GridLiance West is proposing revisions to Sections 10.1 and 10.4 to 
clarify that the Eligible Customer is the entity that requests Interconnection on behalf of a Large 
Load.25 GridLiance West, as the interconnecting PTO, will perform the System Impact Study and 
Facilities Study for the Eligible Customer taking transmission service on behalf of a Large Load 
pursuant to Section 10.26  As part of its study obligations, GridLiance West will apprise CAISO 
of Large Load interconnections through its inputs to the Base Case, Interconnection Studies, and 
the Transmission Planning Process.27  Prior to energization of any Large Load, GridLiance West 
must provide CAISO the information required by Section 25.7.1 of the CAISO Tariff, and the 
Eligible Customer must provide that information to GridLiance West and notify GridLiance West 
of any material changes within 10 Business Days.28  
Furthermore, GridLiance West proposes new Section 10.5.1 to clarify additional 
application requirements for Large Load interconnections.  Specifically, an Eligible Customer 
seeking to interconnect a Large Load must submit: (i) the Large Load’s ramp schedule, 
identifying load additions over time and maximum planned load; (ii) a site plan; (iii) 
documentation of the local, state, and federal permits and regulatory approvals necessary to 
develop the Large Load; (iv) documentation demonstrating Site Control; (v) a single-line 
electrical diagram; (vi) information on any other Interconnection requests made on behalf of the 
same Large Load or its affiliates; (vii) whether the Large Load intends to request Partial Interim 
Service or FILI Service; and (viii) for a Large Load co-located with a Generating Facility, 
information sufficient for GridLiance West to ensure compliance with Sections 25.1.1, 25.7.5, 
and 25.7.6 of the CAISO Tariff.  Because Section 10.4 requires every Interconnection 
Application to be copied to CAISO, Section 10.5.1(vi) requires disclosure of other pending 
requests on behalf of the same Large Load to CAISO, as the Commission contemplated.29  
GridLiance West and CAISO, as applicable, must determine whether an application is complete 
within ten (10) Business Days under Section 10.6. 
An applicant must pay a $5,000 nonrefundable Large Load Interconnection Application 
fee.30  At the time of application, they must provide site plans, demonstration of Site Control

(which is newly defined to ensure control of the site), and receipt of necessary permits.31  These 
requirements will ensure that interconnection applications are real, concrete, and nonspeculative.  
Furthermore, GridLiance West proposes that, at the Large Load System Impact Study phase, the 
Eligible Customer must provide a refundable study deposit of: (a) $35,000 plus $1,000 per MW 
for Interconnection Applications less than 80 MW; (b) $150,000 for Interconnection Applications 
greater than or equal to 80 MW but less than 200 MW; or (c) $250,000 for Interconnection 
Applications greater than 200 MW.32 The refundable study deposit amounts are consistent with 
those required in CAISO’s generator interconnection process.  At the Facilities Study phase, the 
Eligible Customer must pay the estimated cost of the Facilities Study, and, before energization, 
amongst other requirements, it must execute the Interconnection Agreement and pro forma Cost 
Recovery Agreement, and post all required financial security (Sections 10.17.2, 8.1.5.1(viii), and 
13.2.1).  These readiness requirements thus escalate at distinct phases throughout the study 
process, consistent with the Show Cause Order directives.33  An applicant that withdraws from 
the process at any phase must reimburse GridLiance West for all costs reasonably incurred and 
may be responsible for the cost of restudying later-queued applicants.  
For a Large Load Interconnection, the System Impact Study must evaluate the Large 
Load’s operational characteristics, including its ramp schedule, its performance during system 
disturbances, and any ability to limit its withdrawals from the CAISO Controlled Grid, consistent 
with Section 25.7.1 of the CAISO Tariff.  The PTO will evaluate impacts to the transmission 
system using power flow and short circuit analyses, and any other analyses that may be 
appropriate including Electromagnetic Transient studies where warranted.  The completed 
System Impact Study will include a non-binding, good-faith estimate of the cost of Direct 
Assignment Facilities and Network Upgrades needed to accommodate the request and the time 
required to construct them, which the Facilities Study then refines.  GridLiance West may 
request additional information, data, or models reasonably needed for the study, including 
models suitable for Electromagnetic Transient studies.  The request then proceeds through 
GridLiance West’s existing Facilities Study procedures, which refine the facilities design and the 
cost and schedule estimates for incorporation into the Interconnection Agreement. 
3. 
Operational and Reliability Requirements  
Commission Concerns:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the CAISO Tariff and PTO Tariffs appear to be unjust and unreasonable because they 
lack appropriate provisions regarding the ongoing operational requirements that will apply to 
transmission customers serving Large Loads.34  The Commission further highlighted the lack of 
detail on data available to CAISO regarding interconnected Large Loads for monitoring and 
reliability purposes, the lack of language enabling CAISO to remotely disconnect Large Loads

via installed equipment, the absence of specified ramp rate, ride-through, and control 
technologies or protection systems required.35  
GridLiance West Solution:  It is GridLiance West’s understanding that CAISO is 
proposing changes to Section 25.7.1 of the CAISO Tariff to provide substantial additional clarity 
regarding ongoing operational requirements for Eligible Customers serving Large Loads, 
including Frequency Ride-Through, Voltage Ride-Through, Post-Fault Active Power Recovery, 
and Ramp-Rate Limitation requirements.  Accordingly, GridLiance West’s proposed Section 
10.17 specifies that any Large Load Interconnection Agreement will require compliance with 
Section 25.7.1 of the CAISO Tariff, and proposed Section 10.3 requires GridLiance West to 
provide the information required by Section 25.7.1 to CAISO prior to energization of the Large 
Load.  This approach will ensure that Large Load operational requirements remain current with 
CAISO standards and provide transparency and regularity of operational standards that will 
support reliable operation of the overall grid.   
GridLiance West also proposes a series of additional operational requirements mirroring 
CAISO Tariff measures, specifically:  
 Following proposed CAISO Tariff Section 25.7.4 by requiring the Eligible 
Customer, Large Load, Scheduling Coordinator, and GridLiance West to comply 
with any CAISO, Regional Entity, or Reliability Coordinator data request after a 
disturbance or other reliability event involving a Large Load (Section 16.12); 
 Ensuring visibility into Large Load operations by extending proposed CAISO 
Tariff Section 25.7.3 requirements for the Scheduling Coordinator for each Large 
Load to provide daily and hourly forecasts, material real-time deviations, outage 
information, and real-time telemetry (Sections 8.1.5.1(iii) and 10.17); and 
 Following proposed CAISO Tariff Sections 25.7.1.1, 25.7.1.2, 25.7.1.3, and 
25.7.1.4, by requiring Large Load to meet all frequency ride-through 
requirements, voltage ride through requirements, post-fault active power recovery 
requirements, and ramp rate limitations established therein (Section 8.1.5.1(x)). 
Finally, GridLiance West proposes requirements for installation and maintenance of the 
equipment required to disconnect or otherwise isolate the Large Load (Sections 8.1.5.1(vi) and 
10.17), with those costs directly assigned to the applicant to avoid cost shifting to transmission 
customers (Section 8.1.2). 
4. 
Alternative Transmission Technologies   
Commission Concerns:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the CAISO Tariff and PTO Tariffs appear to be unjust and unreasonable because they 
lack clear and consistent provisions requiring the evaluation of alternative transmission 
technologies as potential solutions to an Eligible Customer’s request for service on behalf of a 
 
35  Id. at P 63.

10 
Large Load,36 or requiring an explanation to the Eligible Customer why alternative transmission 
technologies are not feasible or would not result in lower costs or a faster timeline 
accommodating the request.37  
GridLiance West Solution:  The proposed revisions to Section 10.12.1 commit 
GridLiance West to considering alternative transmission technologies in the System Impact 
Study for every Large Load Interconnection Application, without the need for a request from the 
Eligible Customer.  If GridLiance West selects traditional Network Upgrades instead, it must 
demonstrate why alternative transmission technologies are not feasible or would not result in 
lower costs or a faster timeline for accommodating the request.38  This provision is consistent 
with the proposed revision to CAISO Tariff Section 24.1, which extends CAISO’s consideration 
of alternative transmission technologies to Large Loads and contemplates the inclusion of similar 
language in the PTO Tariffs. 
5. 
Study Process Timeline 
Commission Concerns:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the study processes could culminate in a report to the Eligible Customer describing 
the Network Upgrades necessary to accommodate the service request as well as a non-binding 
good-faith estimate of the cost and the time to construct such facilities, which should take no 
more than 60-90 days calendar days to complete.39  
GridLiance West Solution:  GridLiance West proposes the adoption of revised Section 
10.12 and 10.12.1 to its tariff requiring that a System Impact Study for a Large Load provide a 
non-binding, good-faith estimate of the cost of Direct Assignment Facilities and Network 
Upgrades needed to accommodate the request and a similar good-faith time estimate required to 
construct them.  Following the System Impact Study, pursuant to Section 10.16 the Facilities 
Study will refine those estimates leading into the Interconnection Agreement process.40  The 
report will be available following the System Impact Study, consistent with the Show Cause 
Order directive.  
GridLiance West also recognizes the need for timely progression of required studies.  
Accordingly, the proposed GridLiance West Tariff revisions shorten the timeline for 
interconnection studies at each step of the process to the maximum extent achievable (Sections 
10.8 - 10.12).  Under the proposed Large Load study procedures, GridLiance West must notify 
the applicant whether a System Impact Study is required within ten (10) Business Days of the 
Completed Application Date and must tender a System Impact Study Agreement within ten (10) 
Business Days of receipt of the Completed Interconnection Application.  The applicant must 
execute that agreement within ten (10) Business Days and, for a Large Load Interconnection, 
remit a study deposit together with financial security drawable to cover System Impact Study

costs and, if necessary, Facilities Study costs.  GridLiance West must complete the System 
Impact Study no later than ninety (90) Calendar Days after the Completed Application Date.  
This 90-day timeline runs from the Completed Application Date, not from execution of the 
System Impact Study Agreement, and therefore includes the time for the System Impact Study 
Agreement and deposit steps.  The result of this proposed schedule is the initiation and 
completion of a System Impact Study within the 60-90 calendar day range that the Commission 
identified as reasonable.  
 
This proposed structure is consistent with the study process the Commission accepted for 
Southwest Power Pool, Inc.’s (“SPP”) High Impact Large Loads (“HILL”).  For that process, 
SPP must complete its HILL Delivery Point Study and issue a study report within 90 calendar 
days after receiving the executed study agreement, study data, and deposit.41  That study uses 
power flow and short circuit analyses; SPP then performs an Electromagnetic Transient study 
only when those analyses identify system weaknesses caused by the Large Load, similar to 
GridLiance West’s Large Load System Impact Study process.42  The HILL Delivery Point Study 
works “in conjunction with” SPP’s existing load connection study requirements.43  It is followed, 
as needed, by a supplemental load connection study performed by the host transmission owner 
and by SPP’s existing processes for obtaining long-term transmission service.  SPP’s tariff does 
not subject those later steps to the 90-day deadline,44 but the Commission found this process just 
and reasonable.45  GridLiance West’s approach follows the same structure.  A time-certain 
System Impact Study culminates in a report within 90 days, and that report gives the Eligible 
Customer the information the Show Cause Order requires. 
B. 
Co-Located Load  
Commission Concerns:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the CAISO Tariff appears to be unjust and unreasonable because it lacks sufficiently 
clear and consistent tariff provisions addressing the rates, terms, and conditions that apply to co-
location arrangements.46  
GridLiance West Solution:  As acknowledged by the Commission in its Show Cause

D. 
Cost Shifting and Cost Recovery Agreements 
Commission Concern:  In the Show Cause Order, the Commission made a preliminary 
finding that the CAISO Tariff and PTO Tariffs appear to be unjust and unreasonable because they 
lack adequate mechanisms to mitigate the risk of cost shifting among transmission customers.54  
The Show Cause Order directed the PTOs to address: (i) assignment of the Network Upgrade 
costs and their associated costs, that are needed to provide transmission service to Eligible 
Customers serving Large Loads; (ii) the need for a pro forma cost recovery agreement to 
mitigate the risk of cost shifting; and (iii) a mechanism to ensure that any payments attributable 
to the Large Load are appropriately credited toward the PTO’s TRR and documented in the 
annual informational filing for formula rates.55  The Commission also indicated a response 
should clarify how the minimum contribution and financial security required by an Eligible 
Customer serving a Large Load is calculated, i.e., whether by a per-MW figure or another 
methodology.56 
GridLiance West Solution:  Through Section 10.17.2, GridLiance West will utilize a 
Cost Recovery Agreement in the form of Attachment A to the GridLiance West Tariff to address 
assignment of costs associated with the construction and operation of any Network Upgrades 
resulting from the Interconnection of the Large Load.  The Cost Recovery Agreement will be 
between GridLiance West and the Eligible Customer, and CAISO may join at its election.57  The 
Cost Recovery Agreement requires the Eligible Customer to pay 100 percent of the actual costs 
of the Large Load Network Upgrades through the Total Required Revenue Commitment.  The 
Total Required Revenue Commitment establishes both the obligation to pay actual costs and the

CAISO’s Access Charges to cover the Eligible Customer’s Annual Required Revenue 
Commitment, the Eligible Customer must provide Cost Recovery Payments58 to fill the gap in

their Network Upgrades.  GridLiance West will provide a separate workpaper in the

The Cost Recovery Agreement also provides that the required amount of financial

event of non-payment, termination, cancellation, or withdrawal to ensure that the Large Load is

GridLiance West has not proposed to allow an Eligible Customer to satisfy the financial 
security required under the Cost Recovery Agreement with credit support posted under a retail 
agreement.  The Commission’s preliminary finding that an Eligible Customer “may include” 
such security permits this approach but does not require it.59  The approach does not fit a Non-
LSE PTO.  GridLiance West has no retail customers and is not party to any retail service 
agreement.  Any retail security would be held by a third-party load-serving entity, would secure 
that entity’s retail obligations, and be subject to that entity’s draw rights and priorities, none of 
which GridLiance West can control or enforce.  Such security therefore would not be sufficient 
to secure the Eligible Customer’s obligations under the Cost Recovery Agreement.  Accepting it 
would leave other transmission customers exposed to the cost-shifting risk the Order is intended 
to prevent.  The concern about duplicative credit requirements also does not arise here.  The 
security required under the Cost Recovery Agreement secures a separate, Commission-
jurisdictional payment obligation owed to GridLiance West, not the retail obligation owed to the 
load-serving entity.  Requiring a single form of security held directly by the transmission owner 
is also simpler to administer and applies uniformly.

IV. 
RESPONSES TO THE COMMISSION’S REMAINING BRIEFING QUESTIONS 
The Show Cause Order requested responses to specific briefing questions.72  Consistent 
with the division of responsibilities between CAISO and the PTOs recognized by the 
Commission in the Show Cause Order, GridLiance West responds to those briefing questions 
applicable to it as a PTO and defers to CAISO on those questions directed to CAISO or that 
concern matters governed by the CAISO Tariff.  
In the Show Cause Order, the Commission recognized that the framework under which 
CAISO provides transmission service is unique among the RTOs/ISOs and that certain 
responsibilities fall to the PTOs.  The Commission explained that the PTOs “have responsibility 
for wholesale load interconnection studies,” while CAISO “is responsible for access to and the 
provision of transmission service, including transmission and ancillary services, to all Eligible 
Customers, and the reliability of that transmission service.”73  The Commission further 
recognized that the PTOs may be primarily responsible for conducting the studies that evaluate 
whether a Large Load may be interconnected to the transmission system and whether Network 
Upgrades are necessary, that this role stems from how CAISO and the PTOs allocated rights and 
responsibilities in the governing documents establishing CAISO, and that the Commission does 
not seek to alter that allocation of rights and responsibilities.74  Consistent with that framework, 
the Commission directed the PTOs to respond to the extent the matters addressed herein 
implicate aspects of their respective tariffs.75 
Within this framework, GridLiance West’s role is to process and study requests to 
interconnect Eligible Customer Large Loads to its facilities under the GridLiance West Tariff, to 
construct any Direct Assignment Facilities and Reliability Upgrades required for those 
interconnections and recover their costs from the Eligible Customer, and to provide CAISO with 
the necessary information for its operations and its Transmission Planning Process. Transmission 
service over the CAISO Controlled Grid, including GridLiance West’s facilities, is provided by 
CAISO under the CAISO Tariff.  CAISO likewise administers the CAISO Markets and the 
generator interconnection procedures under the CAISO Tariff, and the California Public Utilities 
Commission has primary responsibility for resource adequacy within the CAISO footprint.76 
Moreover, as a Non-LSE PTO, GridLiance West serves no retail load and does not forecast or 
plan for load growth within a retail service territory.   
Accordingly, where a briefing question is directed to CAISO or concerns matters 
governed by the CAISO Tariff, GridLiance West indicates the question is not applicable.  Where 
a briefing question concerns matters within GridLiance West’s responsibilities as a PTO,
